description: Single agent turn that straddles a histogram commitment window boundary. The commitment is made for window N (window_end included in digest), but the long turn spans N and N+1. Per autogen#7888: the digest is honest — it commits to window_end — so a naive verifier must NOT reject the whole turn; the correct handling keeps one receipt per window and exposes the overlap explicitly. Receipt field shape (window_start / outcome / effective) aligns with HeartFlow's WindowAttributionReceipt v0.1.0: effective = the window the turn started in, never post-hoc attribution.

commitment.derivation: hash(histogram, window_end) — window_end is inside the canonicalized preimage, per autogen#7888

cross_implementation.note: Same JSON is validated by Kuberna's verifier and HeartFlow's verifyReceipt() (mark-heartflow-skill, window-attribution-receipt v0.1.0) so both implementations stay honest against each other. effective = start window is a hard invariant on both sides.

handling.naive_verifier: rejects the whole turn — sees steps with timestamps after window_end and assumes forgery
handling.correct_handling: split at the boundary: emit one receipt for window N (steps 0-2) and one for window N+1 (steps 3-4), each against its own commitment digest
handling.overlap_exposed: both receipts carry the same turn_id and boundary timestamp, so a verifier can reconstruct the straddle explicitly instead of forcing a single attribution
handling.effective_attribution: effective = N for both receipts — the window the turn started in; the overlap window N+1 is exposed but never claims attribution
